title: Standardization sits at the execution layer while strategic freedom sits at the Prime Agent layer
content:
A.1.14.2.9 draws the contrast explicitly: "Unlike Prime Agent Artifacts, Executor Agent Artifacts are standardized and come with specific limitations regarding Sky Primitives Activation." A.1.14.2.9.1 enumerates the permitted set — all Genesis Primitives (Agent Creation, Agent Token, Prime Transformation, Executor Transformation), the Operational Primitives (Executor Accord, Root Edit, Light Agent) and "the Executor's own version of the Upkeep Primitive."

Against that, A.1.14.3.1 gives Prime Agents "the autonomy to pursue a unique strategy, model, or method of operations, as defined in their Agent Artifact," subject only to Sky Core Atlas adherence, and A.1.14.2.9.2 confines Executor Artifacts to "each Agent's approach to operationalizing the strategy of different Prime Agents, including risk-management and fees."

The placement of the constraint is the finding. Variety is permitted where it is cheap to contain — strategy, which is business logic — and forbidden where it is expensive, namely the layer holding privileged access to Sky Protocol resources. Since A.1.14.3.4 routes all protocol interaction through Executors, standardizing Executors standardizes the entire attack surface between Agents and the Protocol without constraining what Agents may attempt.

It also makes Executors substitutable. A Prime whose Executor terminates can move to another because Executor Artifacts are comparable by construction — which is exactly what A.1.14.5.2.1's transfer-before-exit requirement depends on. Bespoke Executors would make each Prime hostage to its specific operator.
description: Prime Artifacts define unique strategies with bespoke content; Executor Artifacts are standardized and may activate only an enumerated set of Sky Primitives.
